stem: In microbiology, which of the following defines disease?

options.label: A
options.text: Presence of microbes living on or in the body
options.misconception: Equates the presence of microbes (colonization or infection) with disease.
options.explanation: Microbes on or in the body may be normal microbiota, colonization or infection; disease requires damage or impairment of structure or function, not mere presence.

options.label: B
options.text: Presence of antibodies against a specific microbe
options.misconception: Equates serologic evidence of exposure with disease.
options.explanation: Antibodies against a microbe show past or present exposure; they do not by themselves mean body structure or function is impaired.

options.label: C
options.text: Subjective symptoms reported by the patient
options.misconception: Equates disease with symptoms, missing asymptomatic structural or functional damage.
options.explanation: Symptoms are subjective indicators a patient notices; disease is defined by damaged structure or function, which can occur with no symptoms.

options.label: D
options.text: Damage or impairment of normal structure or function
options.misconception: None — disease is damage or impairment of normal body structure or function.
options.explanation: OpenStax defines disease as any condition in which the normal structure or functions of the body are damaged or impaired.

options.label: E
options.text: An abnormal result on a routine screening test
options.misconception: Equates a positive screening test with established disease.
options.explanation: An abnormal screening result is a finding that needs confirmation; it can be a false positive and is not itself the definition of disease.

context: Learning objective: A disease is any condition in which the normal structure or functions of the body are damaged or impaired.
